title: The Banach-Tarski Paradox: How to Double a Ball Without Adding Anything
question: How can a solid ball be cut into pieces and reassembled into two balls identical to the original, with no stretching and no material added?
summary: The Banach-Tarski theorem proves that a solid sphere can be decomposed into a finite number of pieces and reassembled, using only rotations and translations, into two spheres each the same size as the original. It is not a physical possibility but a strict mathematical theorem, and its truth exposes a fault line running through the foundations of mathematics itself: the axiom of choice.
